overview.problem: The parity oracle in tests/baselines/manifest.json covers 8 invocations across 7 subcommands and reaches neither scan-reconnect-candidates nor rewrite-from-reconnect, the two commands the first shared-core refactor touches. The oracle is also unpinned: a regeneration that rewrites the recorded contract leaves no trace a reviewer can check.
overview.approach: A sibling recon/ fixture tree feeds six reconnect cases spanning matched, ambiguous, dangling, dry-run and writing forms. Byte comparison relaxes only where the run directory unavoidably leaks into rewritten LOCATION bytes, through an opt-in normalise_run_root field backed by one shared substitution helper that regenerate.py and the parity test both import. A SHA-256 constant in tests/test_parity_baseline.py pins the manifest's bytes, a meta-test proves the pin bites on a one-character mutation, and an annotated parity-baseline-v1 tag marks the commit. The fingerprint tier stays unpinned, recorded as a gap for a reviewed parity-baseline-v2 re-tag.

decisions.decision: Reconnect fixture NMLs and their audio stubs live in a sibling recon/ tree built by build_reconnect_fixtures(), never under corpus/
decisions.reasoning: compare_cmd.py:95 enumerates a scan root with a recursive nml glob -> any extra .nml under corpus/ counts toward the stored scan-compare-candidates case -> a probe moved candidates_scanned from 6 to 7 -> reconnect fixtures under corpus/ diff a pre-existing baseline entry, while a sibling tree leaves all 8 stored cases byte-identical

decisions.decision: Every reconnect baseline case passes --volume-map and --match-confidence filename explicitly
decisions.reasoning: resolve_volume_identity infers identity from a scan root that prefixes the old records' decoded dirs -> the recon/ scan root is not such a prefix and raises VolumeIdentityError; separately each fixture .mp3 is 16 zero bytes with no readable tags -> the tag-derived confidence tiers cannot fire -> filename_size is the only tier that produces a match, so both flags are pinned in argv rather than left to inference

decisions.decision: Run-root normalisation is opt-in per case via a normalise_run_root manifest field, and the substitution lives in one helper module imported by both regenerate.py and the parity test
decisions.reasoning: rewrite-from-reconnect writing a real match embeds the per-run temp dir in the output NML's LOCATION DIR -> those bytes compare unequal across runs, yet dropping the case leaves the rewritten LOCATION unpinned, which is exactly what the renderer split can break -> substituting the resolved run root with a fixed RUN_ROOT token in both native and Traktor-encoded forms makes the case comparable; opt-in keeps every other case provably strict, and a single helper keeps the writer and the reader from drifting into different substitutions

decisions.decision: The dangling-match rewrite-from-reconnect case is written and compared with zero substitutions
decisions.reasoning: an unmatched record's LOCATION passes through untouched -> its output NML contains no run-root path -> the case is reproducible as-is -> one written-file case is compared with absolute byte-exactness, proving the oracle does not depend on normalisation to pass

decisions.decision: The fingerprint-tier case is absent from parity-baseline-v1 and the gap is recorded as an explicit unpinned tier
decisions.reasoning: HAS_ACOUSTID gates on importing the acoustid Python module rather than on the fpcalc binary -> a stub fpcalc on PATH cannot light the tier, and pyacoustid is not importable here -> captured stdout would differ on a machine that has the module -> the case is machine-dependent; adding pyacoustid and mutagen as test dependencies to close it costs the oracle its machine-independence, so the tier stays unpinned until the direct-Popen commit adds it under a reviewed parity-baseline-v2 re-tag

decisions.decision: PARITY_BASELINE_SHA256 in tests/test_parity_baseline.py is the sole authoritative pin; no tag commit-SHA constant is recorded
decisions.reasoning: the hash constant is checkable by plain pytest with no git dependency -> a tag-SHA constant is unverifiable without git and becomes documentation pytest cannot enforce -> recording it creates a second pin that rots silently; the tag-resolves-to-recorded-SHA assertion belongs with the CI workflow, and this repo carries no CI config

decisions.decision: _OUTPUT_ARG_INDEX carries an entry mapping rewrite-from-reconnect to argv index 2
decisions.reasoning: _output_paths consults that mapping to decide which argument names a written file -> a command absent from the mapping counts as read-only -> rewrite-from-reconnect writes its NML to argv[2], so without the entry the writing forms pin stdout alone and the written bytes escape the oracle

decisions.decision: index_scan_roots statistics stay out of the reconnect cases' stdout, so tag-cache mtime variability never reaches the oracle
decisions.reasoning: _run_reconnection calls index_scan_roots without a stats dict -> cache_hits, cache_misses and files_seen are never printed -> the tag cache keyed on path|size|mtime varies per run without touching any compared byte -> the reconnect cases need no cache suppression flag

decisions.decision: build_reconnect_fixtures is called from regenerate.py and from tests/conftest.py's fixture_corpus
decisions.reasoning: the parity test materialises its inputs through fixture_corpus while regenerate.py builds its own tree -> the reconnect cases read recon/ paths in both -> both call sites build the same tree from the same fixed literals, so a case runs identically under regeneration and under pytest

decisions.decision: The lxml backend is a pinned precondition of the parity oracle rather than a variable it tolerates: regenerate.py refuses to run and both parity test modules refuse to compare when HAS_LXML is False
decisions.reasoning: xmlio.py:16-25 selects lxml or stdlib ET at import time and write_traktor_xml serialises differently on each branch while rewrite.py:433 write_nml_safely takes a different code path per branch (mutate_tree pre-seeds four zeroed stats keys the lxml path never emits) -> the writing cases in DL-003/DL-004 would record a different stdout stats shape and different output bytes on a stdlib-only machine -> the manifest would be valid only on the capture machine -> since README declares lxml a required install (mutagen and pyacoustid optional), the backend is not genuinely variable and can be pinned at zero dependency cost by asserting it at both the writer and the reader, converting a silent machine-dependence into a loud precondition failure

decisions.decision: The machine-dependence standard DL-005 applies to the fingerprint tier is applied identically to the lxml-dependent writing cases; the two resolve differently only because their dependency status differs
decisions.reasoning: both HAS_ACOUSTID and HAS_LXML are import-time capability flags whose value changes captured stdout -> the standard is that no baseline entry may depend on an unpinned machine capability -> acoustid is optional per README so pinning it would mean adding a test dependency the oracle is meant to avoid and the tier is therefore dropped (DL-005) -> lxml is already a required install so pinning it adds nothing and the writing cases are therefore kept under an explicit HAS_LXML precondition (DL-010) -> both outcomes discharge the same standard rather than waiving it for the writing cases

decisions.decision: The parity-baseline-* tag guard ships as a repo-tracked hook script at tests/hooks/pre-push with a documented one-line install step and a pytest check that the script exists and rejects a tag-move refspec
decisions.reasoning: .git/hooks is untracked so a mitigation living only there is unreviewable and unenforceable -> a prose-only mitigation in R-004 has nothing a reviewer or CI can check -> tracking the script under tests/hooks/ makes its refusal logic reviewable in the diff and lets a unit test drive it with a tag-delete and a tag-move refspec on stdin and assert a non-zero exit -> the install step stays manual because git cannot self-install hooks and the pytest hash constant remains the authoritative pin regardless of whether the hook is installed

decisions.decision: Scan-root enumeration order needs no new pinning: diskscan.py:103 already iterates sorted(Path(root).rglob("*")), so candidate order is deterministic across filesystems and platforms. Determinism risk 3 is closed by verification rather than by mitigation, and the sort becomes a recorded precondition of every reconnect baseline case.
decisions.reasoning: The ambiguous reconnect case has multiple candidates in different subdirectories whose stdout order would vary if enumeration followed raw filesystem order -> traktor_nml/diskscan.py:103 wraps rglob in sorted() before the audio-extension filter and the resolved-duplicate skip -> ordering therefore derives from the path strings alone and not from directory entry order -> no manifest field or argv change is needed; instead the sort itself is load-bearing production behaviour that the baseline silently depends on, so it is documented in regenerate.py where a future reviewer will see it while touching the cases.

decisions.decision: rewrite-from-reconnect keeps its ambiguous-match form as a fourth baseline case; it runs with --csv so the ambiguity report is pinned as an output_files entry alongside the rewritten NML; and because that CSV records candidate paths under the run directory the case carries normalise_run_root, making two normalised entries in parity-baseline-v1 rather than one.
decisions.reasoning: planning_context.constraints and task_spec require an ambiguous-match form and the earlier case list dropped it with no rationale -> the ambiguity path is exactly where the shared-core refactor changes reporting shape (the renderer split rewrites how unresolved candidates are printed) so it is the highest-value form to pin -> its distinguishing output is the CSV rather than the NML (an ambiguous entry is reported and left unrewritten) so the case is only meaningful with --csv and the CSV recorded as an output file -> the CSV lists absolute candidate paths under the per-run temp directory so byte-exactness is impossible without the DL-003 run-root substitution -> accept a second normalise_run_root entry and restate the count in M-001 acceptance rather than dropping the form or pinning a CSV that cannot reproduce.

decisions.decision: PARITY_BASELINE_SHA256 may only move together with a reviewed regeneration and a new parity-baseline-vN tag; the rule is stated as an invariant in the plan / in tests/baselines/manifest.schema.md / in tests/baselines/CLAUDE.md and is repeated verbatim in the guard's assertion failure message.
decisions.reasoning: The guard as designed is defeated by a two-line edit: regenerate manifest.json and paste the new digest -> that is precisely the regenerate-to-go-green anti-pattern the oracle exists to prevent (rejected_alternatives entry 3) and no technical control can stop it because both files are ordinary tracked text -> the only available control is making the rule unmissable at the moment of violation - the failing assertion the editor is staring at - and legible at the moment of review -> the message must name both halves of the gate ('reviewed regeneration + new parity-baseline-vN tag') because naming regeneration alone reads as an instruction to regenerate.

decisions.decision: tests/baselines/CLAUDE.md states the required CI check in prose - CI must run tests/test_parity_baseline.py; and any job that diffs manifest.json against parity-baseline-v1 must also assert that tag still resolves to its recorded commit SHA - without authoring any workflow file.
decisions.reasoning: task_spec puts CI workflow authoring out of scope but permits stating the required check -> the tag carries no server-side protection (R-004) so a moved tag silently moves any comparison anchored to it -> a rule that lives only in this session's context dies with the session and the future author of the first workflow has no way to learn it -> writing it as prose in the directory doc the workflow author will read satisfies the requirement without creating the workflow.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Place the reconnect fixture NMLs under corpus/ alongside the existing fixtures
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: A probe showed candidates_scanned moving from 6 to 7 in the stored scan-compare-candidates case, which diffs a pre-existing baseline entry the change is required to leave untouched.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Light up the fingerprint tier with a stub fpcalc binary on PATH, as docs/nicegui-gui-analysis.md 3.1 suggests
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: HAS_ACOUSTID gates on importing the acoustid Python module, not on the binary, so a stub fpcalc leaves the tier dark; the doc's premise does not hold.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Add pyacoustid and mutagen as test dependencies so the fingerprint tier can be baselined now
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: The oracle's machine-independence and freedom from third-party deps outweigh covering an optional tier one commit early.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Normalise the run root in every case unconditionally
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Blanket substitution weakens the seven strict cases to prove nothing about absolute byte-exactness; opt-in confines the relaxation to the one case that needs it.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Skip the writing form that produces a real match and baseline only the dry-run and dangling forms
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: The rewritten LOCATION bytes are the ones the renderer split can break; leaving them unpinned defeats the purpose of task 0.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Record the parity-baseline-v1 commit SHA as a second constant next to PARITY_BASELINE_SHA256
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: pytest cannot check it without a git dependency, so it is documentation masquerading as a pin, and the SHA does not exist until the commit is made.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Gate the baseline in CI with git diff --exit-code on manifest.json
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: It passes on any commit that regenerated and committed the baseline, which is precisely the case the guard exists to catch.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Commit the reconnect cases after the shared-core refactor lands
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: An oracle captured after the change it polices records the changed behaviour, not the behaviour being preserved.

constraints: No file under traktor_nml/ changes: this commit is test, fixture and documentation only
Regenerating manifest.json leaves the 8 pre-existing entries byte-identical
Every added case is deterministic across runs, machines and temp directories
Cases cover scan-reconnect-candidates and rewrite-from-reconnect in dry-run, writing, ambiguous-match and dangling-match forms
tests/test_parity_baseline.py runs under plain pytest with no git dependency
A meta-test proves the hash guard fails on a one-character manifest mutation
An annotated parity-baseline-v1 tag points at the resulting commit and is pushed

risks.risk: Any .nml added under corpus/ perturbs the stored scan-compare-candidates case, since compare_cmd.py enumerates scan roots with a recursive nml glob.
risks.mitigation: Reconnect fixtures live in a sibling recon/ tree; audio stubs under corpus/audio/ were probed and leave the case unchanged.

risks.risk: rewrite-from-reconnect writing a real match embeds the run's absolute temp directory in the output NML's LOCATION DIR, since location_from_disk_path strips only the anchor.
risks.mitigation: The matched writing case carries normalise_run_root; both regenerate.py and the parity test substitute the RUN_ROOT token through the shared helper before comparing.

risks.risk: A --fingerprint case captured where pyacoustid is absent produces different stdout on a machine where it imports, making the entry machine-dependent.
risks.mitigation: The tier stays out of parity-baseline-v1 and the gap is stated in tests/baselines/CLAUDE.md and docs/nicegui-gui-analysis.md 3.1 as work for a reviewed parity-baseline-v2 re-tag.

risks.risk: The parity-baseline-v1 tag carries no server-side protection: GitHub rulesets need Pro or a public repo and the legacy tag-protection API is gone.
risks.mitigation: tests/hooks/pre-push (CI-M-003-004) is tracked in the repo and refuses any push that deletes or moves a parity-baseline-* tag; test_pre_push_hook_refuses_to_move_or_delete_a_parity_baseline_tag (CI-M-003-005) drives it with delete/move/new-tag/branch refspecs, and M-003's acceptance criteria require both the script and the documented install step. The authoritative pin remains the pytest hash constant, which is independent of the tag.

risks.risk: Normalisation applied to the wrong scope masks a genuine regression in the rewritten LOCATION bytes.
risks.mitigation: A meta-test mutates a non-run-root byte of the normalised case's expected output and asserts the comparison still fails.

risks.risk: xmlio.py selects lxml or stdlib ET at import time; write_traktor_xml serialises differently per branch and rewrite.py:433 write_nml_safely runs a different code path whose mutate_tree pre-seeds four zeroed stats keys, so a manifest captured with lxml present mismatches on a stdlib-only machine and would read as a tool regression.
risks.mitigation: CI-M-001-009 makes regenerate.py exit non-zero before writing the manifest when HAS_LXML is False, and CI-M-001-010 fails tests/test_baseline_parity.py at import with an lxml-precondition reason; M-001's acceptance criteria require both to be exercised with HAS_LXML forced False. README already declares lxml a required install so nothing new is depended on.

risks.risk: Determinism risk 3 from context.json: scan-root indexing order could depend on filesystem enumeration order, which would make the multi-candidate ambiguous case's stdout and CSV row order machine-dependent.
risks.mitigation: CLOSED BY VERIFICATION - traktor_nml/diskscan.py:103 iterates sorted(Path(root).rglob("*")), so order derives from path strings alone. CI-M-001-011 records the dependence in regenerate.py: any future change to that sort invalidates every reconnect baseline case.

invisible_knowledge.system: manifest.json is the tool's behavioural contract for a fixed argv list: exit code, stdout and every written file's bytes. regenerate.py writes it, tests/test_baseline_parity.py reads it, tests/test_parity_baseline.py hashes it. The oracle's authority rests on predating the change it polices, so it is captured before the shared-core refactor rather than after.
invariants: Regenerating manifest.json is correct only for a deliberate, reviewed behaviour change, never to make a failing test pass (DL-002/DL-011 in the project's own decision log)
The oracle predates the change it polices
The tag cache is written even under --dry-run by design, being a scan speedup rather than command output
A manifest entry without normalise_run_root is compared with zero substitutions
New .nml fixtures stay out of corpus/, which doubles as a scan root for the compare cases
The parity oracle is captured and compared under the lxml backend only; a stdlib-ET environment fails the precondition loudly rather than producing or comparing manifest bytes (DL-010)
No baseline entry may depend on an unpinned machine capability: a capability that is a required install is pinned (lxml), one that is optional is excluded (acoustid) (DL-011)

PARITY_BASELINE_SHA256 moves only alongside a reviewed regeneration AND a new parity-baseline-vN tag; editing the constant to match a regenerated manifest is the regenerate-to-go-green defect the oracle exists to detect (DL-015). The rule is stated in tests/baselines/manifest.schema.md, in tests/baselines/CLAUDE.md, and verbatim in the guard's assertion failure message, which names both halves so it cannot read as an instruction to regenerate.

Candidate enumeration order is deterministic because traktor_nml/diskscan.py:103 iterates sorted(Path(root).rglob("*")); every reconnect baseline case (stdout ordering and ambiguity-CSV row order) depends on that sort, so changing or removing it is a production behaviour change invalidating all reconnect baselines (DL-013).

Any CI job that diffs manifest.json against the parity-baseline-v1 tag must also assert the tag still resolves to its recorded commit SHA; the tag is only hook-protected, so a moved tag moves the comparison with it (DL-016).
tradeoffs: parity-baseline-v1 carries no server-side protection on this repo; the compensating control is a tracked tests/hooks/pre-push script (manually installed, driven by a test) refusing to move or delete parity-baseline-* tags, and the pytest hash constant is the authoritative pin

One writing case trades absolute byte-exactness for reproducibility via run-root normalisation, while the dangling writing case retains absolute byte-exactness so the oracle's strictness stays demonstrable
The fingerprint tier stays uncovered rather than pulling pyacoustid and mutagen into the test dependencies

code_intents.behavior: Writes a recon/ tree from fixed literal strings under a caller-supplied directory: simple.nml holding one COLLECTION ENTRY whose LOCATION names a stale path, ambiguous.nml holding one ENTRY whose filename matches two stubs in different subdirectories, dangling.nml holding one ENTRY whose filename matches nothing on disk, and a recon/audio tree of 16-zero-byte .mp3 stubs whose sizes match the FILESIZE attributes the filename_size tier compares. Two calls against an empty directory produce byte-identical output.
Materialises the reconnect tree beside the corpus tree in tmp_path, so a manifest case naming recon/ paths resolves under pytest exactly as it does under regeneration.

Substitutes a fixed RUN_ROOT token for every form the run directory takes in captured output: the native absolute path, its forward-slash form, and the Traktor-encoded anchor-stripped form whose separators read slash-colon. The longest form substitutes first, so a shorter form cannot consume a prefix of a longer one. A bytes companion decodes UTF-8, substitutes, and re-encodes, leaving line endings intact.

Carries seven reconnect invocations beyond the eight pre-existing ones: scan-reconnect-candidates over simple.nml, ambiguous.nml and dangling.nml, each writing its own --csv under out/; rewrite-from-reconnect over simple.nml under --dry-run; rewrite-from-reconnect over simple.nml writing its NML; rewrite-from-reconnect over ambiguous.nml writing its NML AND naming --csv out/ambiguous_reconnect.csv, so the ambiguity report is captured as an output_files entry beside the NML and the ambiguous form required by the constraints is pinned rather than dropped; and rewrite-from-reconnect over dangling.nml writing its NML. Every reconnect invocation names --scan-root recon/audio, --volume-map, and --match-confidence filename. The ambiguous writing case is listed in the module's normalise-run-root set because its CSV records candidate paths under the run directory.

Maps rewrite-from-reconnect to argv index 2 alongside the rewrite and rewrite-from-collection-compare entries, so _output_paths captures the NML each writing form produces. For an invocation that also names --csv, the path following that flag is captured as a second output_files entry, so the ambiguous writing case records both the rewritten NML and the ambiguity CSV rather than the NML alone.

Builds the reconnect tree beside the corpus tree in the target directory, and for a case listed in the module's normalise-run-root set writes stdout and every captured output file through the run-root substitution before recording them, emitting a normalise_run_root field on that entry alone. An entry for a case outside the set carries no such field, so the eight pre-existing entries serialise unchanged.

Applies the shared run-root substitution to the captured stdout and to each written file's bytes when the case carries normalise_run_root - covering both the matched-writing NML case and the ambiguous-writing case whose CSV records candidate paths - and compares verbatim otherwise, holding a case without the field to absolute byte-exactness.

Corrupts one byte of the normalised writing case's stored output outside any run-root span and asserts the comparison the parity test makes still fails, proving the substitution relaxes only the run directory.

Refuses to regenerate when traktor_nml.xmlio.HAS_LXML is False: exits non-zero before touching manifest.json with a message naming lxml as a required install and stating that a stdlib-ET capture would record a different stats-key set and a different serialised byte stream for the rewrite-from-reconnect writing cases. This makes the backend a checked precondition of the recorded contract rather than an unrecorded property of the capture machine.

Reads HAS_LXML from traktor_nml.xmlio at import and fails the module with an explicit reason when it is False rather than letting the writing cases mismatch as if the tool had regressed. The reason names lxml as a required install and points at the regenerate guard so a stdlib-only environment cannot be mistaken for a parity failure or silently pass.

A module-level comment beside the reconnect entries in CASES records that every reconnect baseline depends on traktor_nml/diskscan.py:103 iterating sorted(Path(root).rglob("*")): candidate order in stdout and in the ambiguity CSV is that sort's order and nothing else. It states that removing or altering that sort is a production behaviour change which invalidates every reconnect baseline case, so it demands a reviewed regeneration and a new parity-baseline-vN tag rather than a quiet re-capture. This closes Determinism risk 3 by verified fact rather than by mitigation.

+"""Shared substitution helper for the opt-in run-root normalisation.
+
+rewrite-from-reconnect writing a real match embeds the per-run temp
+directory in the output NML's LOCATION DIR: location_from_disk_path
+strips only the resolved candidate path's own anchor (the drive letter
+or POSIX root), never the caller's scan root, so every intermediate path
+segment between the volume root and wherever the fixture corpus happens
+to live for this run ends up in the rewritten DIR (DL-003). Those bytes
+compare unequal across runs, machines and temp directories even though
+nothing about the tool's behaviour changed.
+
+This module is the single definition of what RUN_ROOT_TOKEN replaces,
+imported by both tests/baselines/regenerate.py (the writer) and
+tests/test_baseline_parity.py (the reader), so the two can never drift
+into different substitutions.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from traktor_nml.model import encode_traktor_dir
+
+RUN_ROOT_TOKEN = "RUN_ROOT"
+
+
+def _run_root_forms(run_root: Path) -> list[str]:
+    """Every textual form run_root can take in captured output: the native
+    absolute path, its forward-slash form, and the Traktor-encoded
+    anchor-stripped form location_from_disk_path actually writes into a
+    LOCATION's DIR. Longest first, so a shorter form (the anchor-stripped
+    encoding) can never consume a prefix of a longer one (the native path)
+    during substitution.
+    """
+    resolved = run_root.resolve()
+    native = str(resolved)
+    forward = native.replace("\\", "/")
+    anchor = resolved.anchor
+    relative = resolved.relative_to(anchor) if anchor else resolved
+    relative_str = str(relative)
+    encoded = "/:" if relative_str in ("", ".") else encode_traktor_dir(relative_str)
+    return sorted({native, forward, encoded}, key=len, reverse=True)
+
+
+def normalise_run_root(text: str, run_root: Path) -> str:
+    """Substitute RUN_ROOT_TOKEN for every form run_root takes in text."""
+    for form in _run_root_forms(run_root):
+        if form:
+            text = text.replace(form, RUN_ROOT_TOKEN)
+    return text
+
+
+def normalise_run_root_bytes(data: bytes, run_root: Path) -> bytes:
+    """Bytes companion to normalise_run_root: decodes UTF-8, substitutes,
+    and re-encodes, leaving line endings intact since the substitution
+    itself never touches a line-ending byte."""
+    return normalise_run_root(data.decode("utf-8"), run_root).encode("utf-8")

requirements: A SHA-256 constant pins manifest.json's bytes
The guard runs under plain pytest with no git dependency
The hash-and-compare step is a single helper taking a manifest path so the guard and the meta-test exercise identical code
PARITY_BASELINE_SHA256 may only move alongside a reviewed regeneration and a new parity-baseline-vN tag; the guard's assertion failure message states that rule naming both halves
A meta-test proves a one-character on-disk manifest mutation fails the guard

Altering one character of manifest.json on disk makes test_manifest_matches_pinned_hash fail
The meta-test copies the manifest to tmp_path / mutates one character on disk / and drives the guard's own comparison against that copy
The guard's failure message contains the words 'reviewed regeneration' and 'new parity-baseline-vN tag'
The module imports nothing from git and starts no subprocess

Meta: an on-disk one-character mutation of a tmp_path copy makes the shared helper raise

code_intents.behavior: Holds the hex SHA-256 of tests/baselines/manifest.json's bytes as the authoritative pin on the oracle's contents.

Exposes the hash-and-compare step as a helper taking the manifest path - _assert_manifest_matches(path) - which reads the file's bytes, hashes them, and asserts equality with PARITY_BASELINE_SHA256. test_manifest_matches_pinned_hash calls it with the committed tests/baselines/manifest.json path, so the guard's real comparison is a single definition that the meta-test can drive against any path. The assertion failure message states that manifest.json no longer matches its pin and that the constant may only move alongside a reviewed regeneration and a new parity-baseline-vN tag - naming both halves so the message cannot read as an instruction to regenerate. Reads only the filesystem: no git import and no subprocess.

Copies tests/baselines/manifest.json into tmp_path, mutates exactly one character of the copy ON DISK, and invokes the same _assert_manifest_matches helper against the mutated copy, asserting it raises. Because the helper is the identical code path test_manifest_matches_pinned_hash runs, the acceptance criterion's literal wording - a one-character on-disk mutation makes that named test fail - is what the meta-test verifies, rather than an in-memory comparison of two strings. The committed manifest is never written to.

+#!/bin/sh
+# Refuses to push a delete or a move of any refs/tags/parity-baseline-* ref.
+#
+# GitHub rulesets need Pro or a public repo and the legacy tag-protection API
+# has been removed, so this hook is the only available control - a speed
+# bump local to one clone, not a control against a determined push
+# (bypassable with --no-verify). The authoritative pin remains
+# PARITY_BASELINE_SHA256 in tests/test_parity_baseline.py, which does not
+# depend on this hook or on the tag at all.
+#
+# Install (git cannot self-install hooks):
+#   cp tests/hooks/pre-push .git/hooks/pre-push && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-push
+
+zero="0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"
+status=0
+
+while read local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha; do
+    case "$remote_ref" in
+        refs/tags/parity-baseline-*)
+            if [ "$local_sha" = "$zero" ]; then
+                echo "refusing to delete protected tag: $remote_ref" >&2
+                status=1
+            elif [ "$remote_sha" != "$zero" ] && [ "$remote_sha" != "$local_sha" ]; then
+                echo "refusing to move protected tag: $remote_ref" >&2
+                status=1
+            fi
+            ;;
+    esac
+done
+
+exit $status

+def test_pre_push_hook_refuses_to_move_or_delete_a_parity_baseline_tag() -> None:
+    """Drives tests/hooks/pre-push with delete/move/new-tag/branch refspecs
+    on stdin and asserts its exit code for each - the same refusal logic a
+    developer's manually-installed .git/hooks/pre-push runs against a real
+    push (see tests/baselines/CLAUDE.md for the install step). Skips rather
+    than fails where no POSIX shell is available, so the suite stays green
+    on a bare Windows checkout while the script itself stays reviewable in
+    the diff."""
+    import shutil
+    import subprocess
+
+    shell = shutil.which("sh")
+    if shell is None:
+        pytest.skip("no POSIX shell available to drive tests/hooks/pre-push")
+
+    hook = Path(__file__).parent / "hooks" / "pre-push"
+    zero = "0" * 40
+    old_sha = "1" * 40
+    new_sha = "2" * 40
+

+        result = subprocess.run([shell, str(hook)], input=refspec, capture_output=True, text=True)
+        return result.returncode
+

+    assert _run(f"refs/tags/parity-baseline-v1 {new_sha} refs/tags/parity-baseline-v1 {old_sha}\n") != 0
+    assert _run(f"refs/tags/parity-baseline-v2 {new_sha} refs/tags/parity-baseline-v2 {zero}\n") == 0
